text: Seven mart columns are affected, as a value or an influence. Direct: mart.fact_po_line.savings_amt (value, derived). Through intermediate tables: mart.po_supplier_summary.total_savings, mart.supplier_spend.total_savings, mart.shipment_fact.ext_amount_usd (via pg_temp.stg_ship), mart.shipment_fact.gross_margin_usd (via pg_temp.stg_ship), mart.customer_snapshot.lifetime_revenue, and mart.customer_snapshot.segment (conditional value, influenced via cust_metrics.segment_hint). Filter edges onto mart.shipment_fact and mart.customer_snapshot bound the whole table, so they are not counted as column impacts. Other affected targets are result sets or temp tables. I did not run a gaps check, so I can't say whether any boundary or refusal limits this trace.

Dropping s2p.po_distribution.amount_cancelled affects 9 mart columns in 3 tables. mart.fact_po_line (direct, value, conditional): line_amt, savings_amt, should_cost. mart.po_supplier_summary (indirect): total_spend (value, aggregated), total_savings (value, aggregated), spend_rank (influence). mart.supplier_spend (indirect): total_spend (value, aggregated), total_savings (value, aggregated), spend_rank (influence). The column is also a filter on which rows land in mart.fact_po_line (edge a1d66c2b125fbae6a8cba436), which is not a value or influence and is not counted in the list. It also feeds the result columns of medium/m1_procurement_savings.sql, which are not mart columns. No boundaries or refusals on this lineage.

mart.po_supplier_summary.total_spend is fed by one value edge: an aggregated (pre-aggregation) edge from mart.fact_po_line.line_amt (bdfa0cdbea618eeb3f02b1f8, h2_po_fact_load.sql:345). mart.fact_po_line.line_amt is fed by five source columns, all with a conditional transform (h2_po_fact_load.sql:31). Nothing feeds any of the five, so they are the ultimate sources:
1. s2p.po_distribution.amount_cancelled
2. s2p.po_distribution.amount_ordered
3. s2p.po_distribution.quantity_cancelled
4. s2p.po_distribution.quantity_ordered
5. s2p.po_line.matching_basis
6. s2p.po_line_location.price_override

That is six columns, not five. I ignored filter and influence edges, as you asked for value flow only. gaps found no boundaries or refusals on this lineage.

The value lineage of total_spend runs from s2p.po_distribution, s2p.po_line and s2p.po_line_location into mart.fact_po_line.line_amt, then into mart.po_supplier_summary.total_spend. The graph holds no filter edges on the s2p source tables themselves. The filtering columns are on the two mart tables.

Two things to know about this list. The filters on mart.fact_po_line apply to the whole table, so they bound total_spend even though some columns, such as the gold.dim_status ones, feed only status_code and not line_amt. The upstream query went 10 hops but returned edges only to depth 2. No boundaries or refusals were reported.

Yes. mart.shipment_fact.gross_margin_usd is traceable to base columns with no boundary or refusal on its lineage. It is loaded from pg_temp.stg_ship.gross_margin_usd by two statements, at lines 106 and 121 of hard/h4_nightly_load.sql, both identity copies. The staging column is built at line 40 from these base columns by value flow:
- lgx.shipment_line.shipped_qty (derived)
- lgx.shipment_line.unit_selling_price (derived)
- lgx.item_master.std_cost (derived)
- gold.fx_rate.conversion_rate (derived)
- gold.fx_rate.to_ccy (conditional)

Other columns affect the value without being part of it. gold.fx_rate.from_ccy, rate_date and loaded_at are influences, not value sources, so I left them out.

The only refusal in the file is line 196, a TRUNCATE of mart.load_audit. That table is not on this lineage, so it doesn't limit the answer.
